context.description:
Figaro Culinary Group Inc. (FCG), formerly Figaro Coffee Group Inc., was incorporated on July 6, 2018 as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Carmetheus Holdings, Inc. primarily to process, manufacture, package all kinds of food products, and establish, invest, develop, operate and maintain restaurants, coffee shops and refreshments parlors, among others.

FCG has one subsidiary, Figaro Coffee Systems, Inc. (FCSI), through which it operates and/or franchises a network of retail restaurants. These include Figaro Coffee, a coffee shop with domestic and international branches; Angel's Pizza, a pizza store chain; Tien Ma's, a Taiwanese cuisine restaurant; Koobideh Kebab, a Mediterranean restaurant; and Café Portofino, an outlet which primarily serves beverages and snacks.

As of June 30, 2024, FCSI operates 60 Figaro coffee shops, 127 Angel's Pizza outlets, 13 Tien Ma's Taiwanese cuisine, one Koobideh Kebab, and five Café Portofino outlet.

Source: SEC Form 17-A (2024)

## Company: Figaro Culinary Group, Inc.  (FCG)
Sector: Industrial / Food, Beverage & Tobacco
Figaro Culinary Group Inc. (FCG), formerly Figaro Coffee Group Inc., was incorporated on July 6, 2018 as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Carmetheus Holdings, Inc. primarily to process, manufacture, package all kinds of food products, and establish, invest, develop, operate and maintain restaurants, coffee shops and refreshments parlors, among others.

FCG has one subsidiary, Figaro Coffee Systems, Inc. (FCSI), through which it operates and/or franchises a network of retail restaurants. These include Figaro Coffee, a coffee shop with domestic and international branches; Angel's Pizza, a pizza store chain; Tien Ma's, a Taiwanese cuisine restaurant; Koobideh Kebab, a Mediterranean restaurant; and Café Portofino, an outlet which primarily serves beverages and snacks.

As of June 30, 2024, FCSI operates 60 Figaro coffee shops, 127 Angel's Pizza outlets, 13 Tien Ma's Taiwanese cuisine, one Koobideh Kebab, and five Café Portofino outlet.

Source: SEC Form 17-A (2024)

storedThesis:
Figaro Culinary Group is a Philippine multi-brand F&B operator whose story is, in practice, almost entirely Angel's Pizza. That chain — 127 outlets as of mid-2024 — generates over 90% of group revenue. The Figaro Coffee brand (60 shops) and the satellite concepts (Tien Ma's, Koobideh Kebab, Café Portofino) are relatively marginal. The business is straightforward to understand: it franchises and operates food-service chains in the Philippines, earns revenue from company-owned stores plus franchise fees, and now aims to add a manufacturing/export leg through its PEZA-registered subsidiary Figaro Innovation and Development Inc. (FIDI). The strategic pivot from "coffee group" to "culinary group" — formalized via a February 2025 rebrand — reflects this broadening ambition honestly.

The moat question is where FCG gets difficult. Angel's Pizza competes directly with Shakey's, Yellow Cab, Greenwich, and Pizza Hut in a market where brand switching is easy and delivery aggregators commoditize convenience. FCG's advantage is operational: Angel's Pizza has successfully penetrated mid-market price points and built suburban/provincial density that international brands haven't fully captured. That is a real edge, but it is an operational and cost-advantage moat at best — not a brand monopoly with strong pricing power. The coffee segment faces an even tougher competitive set (Starbucks, local specialty chains), and the remaining concepts are negligible in scale. FIDI's export manufacturing ambitions are early-stage and unproven; PEZA registration is a positive signal but not yet a revenue driver.

Management shows a pattern worth respecting. The Angel's Pizza spin-off — carving out the asset that generates 90% of revenue into a dedicated entity (Angel's Pizza Inc.) — received SEC approval in July 2026. The stated rationale (operational focus, structural flexibility for domestic and international expansion) is coherent, not defensive. Dividend payments have been consistent, and the manufacturing buildout is being done through a properly structured PEZA enterprise rather than as an ad hoc venture. No major governance red flags appear in the disclosures. The risk is execution: management is juggling a spinoff, a manufacturing ramp, and a weakening core growth rate simultaneously, which demands more organizational bandwidth than a 206-outlet operator typically has.

Valuation is the sticking point. FY2025 revenue was ₱5.67 billion, growing just 4.1% — a dramatic deceleration from the 32% historical average that inflates the 10-year EPS and revenue growth figures in the model. The 10-year metrics embed years of rapid expansion that are no longer the base case. At ₱0.61, the stock is priced at 5.1x earnings and at book value, which looks cheap on a trailing basis. The Rule #1 sticker price of ₱0.72 implies the stock is not dramatically overpriced, but at ₱0.61 it sits 69% above the 50% margin-of-safety buy price of ₱0.36. Phil Town's framework demands that gap for a reason: Angel's Pizza spinoff mechanics mean FCG shareholders will hold shares in a post-restructured parent whose revenue composition is now uncertain, plus whatever stake structure emerges from the spin-off. Paying close to sticker when structural change is mid-flight, growth is decelerating, and FCF data is unavailable does not qualify as a margin-of-safety entry.

The bottom line is watch. This is not a pass — the business is real, the brand has penetration, management is active and appears honest, and the manufacturing optionality is a genuine free call if FIDI delivers. But the margin of safety is absent at ₱0.61. The spinoff creates a transitional period where earnings attribution and growth trajectory will be murky. Wait for the Angel's Pizza spin-off to close and the post-restructure financials to clarify the new FCG parent's standalone profile; if Angel's Pizza eventually lists separately, evaluate it on its own terms. Revisit FCG if the price corrects toward ₱0.40–0.45 and the spinoff-adjusted earnings picture confirms growth re-acceleration.
